name: akshada-Git/Explainable-Diabetes-Risk-Prediction
dataset: Real Pima. Not committed; config lists 3 public mirrors tried in order; schema validated.
models: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest (balanced), XGBoost if installed; 5-fold GridSearchCV on the training split; chosen by CV ROC-AUC.
preprocessing: Zeros -> missing, median imputer + scaler inside a Pipeline; stratified 80/20.
ui: Streamlit app; plain-language summary; PDF report.
extras: SHAP with explicit unit handling and an additivity check; 26 test functions; a minimum-ROC-AUC sanity gate; FRD/PRD/TRD documents.
useful: Explicit SHAP units + additivity check; a sanity gate on test AUC; written requirements documents.
avoid: Do not copy its code or wording: its requirement text is almost identical to ours, so similar wording would look like copying. Write our own, and cite it if we read it.
missing: No SQLite/history, no Gaussian Naive Bayes, no LIME, no calibration/Brier, no data-hash check, no repeated-split stability study.

name: anandd46/DiabetesRiskPrediction_AI
dataset: SYNTHETIC. The generator draws features from normal/Poisson/gamma distributions 'modelled loosely on' Pima statistics and creates the label from a logistic formula. Any metric describes how well a model recovers that formula, not real patients.
models: Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree; scaler fitted on the training split but saved as a separate file.
preprocessing: Scaling only (synthetic data has no real missingness).
extras: SHAP (Tree/Linear explainers); SQLite prediction_history table with parameterised queries; invalid-input tests (age 200, BMI -5); rule-based advice text.
useful: Parameterised SQL, a small repository class, and tests with invalid inputs.
avoid: Synthetic data presented next to Pima; scaler and model saved separately; advice text that reads like medical guidance.
missing: Not real Pima data; no cross-validation; no Gaussian Naive Bayes.

name: UznetDev/Diabetes-Prediction
models: Random Forest (depth 6, 300 trees, entropy) in a Pipeline with custom feature engineering and weight-of-evidence encoding.
preprocessing: Feature engineering + WoE encoding; only 5 of the 8 inputs are used.
ui: Multi-page Streamlit; SHAP waterfall and force plots; README links a live demo (not checked).
deployment: Live Streamlit demo linked in README (not checked).
avoid: It fits the model on ALL rows and prints ROC-AUC on the same rows; the metrics shown in the app are in-sample; a notebook cell scores rows already seen in training.
missing: No honest hold-out report, no tests, no history.

name: pranavppramod/Diabetes-Prediction-System
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
dataset: 768 x 9 with Pima column names, but 652 cells replaced: each missing value holds ONE constant per class (e.g. Glucose 107 / 140). The label is written into the features.
models: Logistic Regression baseline in a scaler Pipeline; Random Forest (200 trees) with GridSearchCV; 5-fold CV.
extras: SHAP explainer saved with joblib; 10 tests; clean src/ split; honest 'tuning did not help' note.
useful: Clean separation of prediction and explainability modules; tests; honesty about failed tuning.
avoid: The dataset file; presenting 0.9458 as Pima performance. README numbers (LR accuracy 70.78 %, AUC 82.63 %; RF AUC 94.58 %) reproduce EXACTLY on its CSV - the RF figure disappears (AUC 0.8168) on the genuine data.
missing: No SQLite/history; imputation not inside a leak-safe pipeline; no Gaussian NB.

name: Faiyaz-48/diabetes-prediction-system
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
models: Logistic Regression (C=1) and Random Forest (200 trees, depth 6), each in a scaler Pipeline; stratified 80:20; joblib.
preprocessing: Zeros -> missing, but filled with the CLASS-CONDITIONAL median (groupby on the label) BEFORE the train/test split.
ui: Five-page Streamlit app (Home, Predict, Dataset Explorer, Model Performance, About); disclaimer 'Educational / academic project only. Not a medical device.'
useful: Input-bounds table and the visible disclaimer.
avoid: Label-dependent imputation before the split: the label leaks into the features and the statistics use test rows. Its committed metrics (RF accuracy 0.8636, AUC 0.942) match what leaked data produce.
missing: No SHAP, no cross-validation, no history, no tests. Widgets allow 0 for Glucose etc., which the model treats as a real value.

name: Vivekrathod01/Diabetes_prediction_system
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
dataset: The same class-conditional pre-imputed Pima file as repository 4 (same 652 replaced cells).
models: LR, KNN, SVM, Gaussian NB, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost (scaler Pipelines); GridSearchCV on RF and XGB.
preprocessing: SMOTE applied AFTER the split on the training part only (correct order).
ui: Streamlit front end with a FastAPI back end.
deployment: Hard-coded Windows path; not deployable as is.
extras: Wide model-comparison table saved as CSV; XGBoost saved with pickle.
useful: A model-comparison CSV; a separate inference API.
avoid: Absolute Windows path, split without stratify, the leaky CSV. Its reported accuracies (LR 0.85, RF 0.88) are inflated by the pre-imputed file; clean Pima gives about 0.71-0.77.
missing: No SHAP, no history, no tests.

name: Niharikaneelu/diabetes_risk_prediction
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
models: Random Forest vs XGBoost; 5-fold CV on the training split.
preprocessing: split_data(leak_free=True) splits first and computes train-only medians; the old leaky path remains reachable with leak_free=False - a nice teaching device.
ui: Streamlit app and a generated static HTML front end.
extras: SHAP (TreeExplainer). Community-reported hold-out (154 rows): RF accuracy 0.7532, AUC 0.8257; XGBoost accuracy 0.7727, AUC 0.8409; CV AUC about 0.828 - realistic.
useful: A flag that switches between the leaky and the leak-free path, to demonstrate the difference.
avoid: Imputation lives outside the saved pipeline, so inference has to re-implement it.
missing: No SQLite/history, no tests, no LIME.

name: Linggge/diabetes-risk-prediction
dataset: Genuine Pima, NOT committed: the app shows 'Dataset not found. Download ...' (good practice).
preprocessing: Zeros -> missing; median SimpleImputer in a ColumnTransformer inside the Pipeline; stratified 80/20.
extras: Metrics computed at runtime; README states it is a cleaned portfolio edition of a university team project and does not claim sole authorship.
useful: Honest authorship statement; graceful behaviour when the dataset is absent.
avoid: Nothing in particular; it is too small to learn much from.
missing: No SHAP, no history, no multi-model comparison, no tests.

name: Arshavir01/diabetes-app
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
models: Linear SVM; pickled model and scaler.
deployment: Live app link in README (not checked).
extras: README reports train accuracy 78.7 % and test accuracy 77.3 % (154 unseen patients) and records two lessons: the scaler must travel with the model, and scikit-learn is pinned (1.6.1) so the pickle loads.
useful: Writing down version-pinning and scaler lessons in the README.
avoid: Loading pickle files from unknown sources can execute code - only load files you created.
missing: Accuracy only; no CV, no SHAP, no history.

name: arunnthevapalan/diabetes-prediction-app
licence: NONE (no LICENSE file) - do not copy
preprocessing: Notebook: class-conditional median imputation; StandardScaler fitted on ALL rows; split without stratify.
useful: Dockerfile as an example of packaging.
avoid: Three protocol problems in the notebook (label-dependent imputation, scaler on all rows, no stratify).
missing: No SHAP, history, CV or tests.

name: CoreyLeath-code/Disease_Prediction_Capstone
dataset: Not Pima-aligned (asks age, BMI, cholesterol, systolic BP; target column 'target'; data not committed).
preprocessing: StandardScaler fitted on the whole matrix before splitting (leakage).
extras: Large engineering scaffold: tests, MODEL_CARD.md, SECURITY.md, ARCHITECTURE.md.
useful: Documentation files (model card, security notes, architecture) as a pattern - not as a Pima example.
avoid: Scaler leakage; do not mistake the scaffolding for a validated diabetes model.
